title: Certified Inference: a pre-registered, exact-real, kernel-checked next-token certificate for a pretrained LayerNorm language model
description:
A pre-registered, independently verifiable statistical certificate for the exact-real next-token argmax of a real pretrained LayerNorm language model — the step where the input space is far too large to enumerate and the honest guarantee becomes statistical rather than exhaustive.

On a pinned finite TinyStories-1M token-id corpus C at context length 16, a with-replacement sample of 1000 prompts was pre-registered — seed and budget committed before any result was seen — and every one certified to have a unique full-vocabulary (50,257-token) exact-real next-token argmax at precision P ≤ 256. By the stated one-sided Hoeffding bound, with confidence ≥ 97.5%, at least 95.70% of C is certifiable under this engine and escalation policy. Every record is re-derived bit-identically by a torch-free checker that asserts full-corpus completeness, so a certificate cannot pass by silently omitting hard prompts.

The statistical wrapper is kernel-checked in Lean 4 with Mathlib (axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound). The kernel earned its keep: it caught a mis-specified tail direction in the project's own task brief before any number was stated. A replication under public pre-commitment (seed 20260704, freeze pushed before any certificate existed, with an OpenTimestamps receipt) reproduced the identical bound. A 300/300 certified calibration table and eight full-vocabulary GPT-2-small certificates are reported as profile and prestige confirmation, carrying no population language.

Scope is stated narrowly and deliberately: the claim quantifies over the pinned finite corpus C only, the certificate concerns the exact-real function of the published weights rather than binary32 execution, and the finite-corpus sampling bridge is audited provenance, not formalised. The wrapper is never described as certified end to end.

This is the third repository of three, continuing verified-circuits and certified-grokking. It does not have the same formal closure as the first two, and does not claim to.

This record archives the repository as of 11 August 2026. The work was first made public on 4 July 2026; the DOI was minted later, so the archive date and the original publication date differ.
